correctness.rationale: For fixed J each marked edge set has n or 2n edges and uniformly bounded candidate conflict degree. Uniform perfect matching probability of t prescribed disjoint edges is the inverse product of the first t odd factors descending from 2n-1; hence spatial joint factorial moments factor with means (1/2,1,...). Conditioning on t edges leaves a uniform matching of n-t chords; crossings among residual edges have the same law as C_{n-t}, and prescribed edges influence at most O_t(n) crossings. The inherited known crossing CLT thus holds uniformly under these rare events, establishing mixed characteristic/factorial moments and independence. Integer maximum-gap tail follows by finite truncation. Enumerating all 146598 matchings through n=7 verified known exact crossing moments and derived covariance, and a triple factorial moment identity.

value.rationale: The maximum circular shorter-arc length is a natural extremal matching invariant. Its exact half-intensity boundary and independent spatial Poisson marks give information absent from a scalar Poisson marginal; pairing the geometric extreme with Gaussian global crossing fluctuations answers a genuinely joint conditional-distribution question. Even though finite covariance has order n, it vanishes on the natural crossing CLT scale. This links localized rare geometry and global graph crossings and yields a usable conditional Gaussian law.
